html:
The Mexica, Mexihcah in Nahuatl, were the people of Tenochtitlan and the leading power of the Triple Alliance that ruled central Mexico in 1492, the state usually called the Aztec Empire. Their island city in Lake Texcoco, founded about 1325, joined Texcoco and Tlacopan in 1428 to overthrow the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco.

Over the next ninety years Mexica rulers such as Itzcoatl, Moctezuma I and Ahuitzotl, who ruled in 1492, led armies to the Gulf coast, Oaxaca and the Pacific. Conquered towns kept their own lords but sent tribute of cloth, food, feathers and cacao, and war captives were sacrificed at the Templo Mayor. Some enemies stayed free, above all Tlaxcala and the Purépecha to the west.

In 1519 Hernán Cortés landed. With Tlaxcalan allies, and with smallpox killing many of the defenders, he took Tenochtitlan in 1521, after Moctezuma II had died in Spanish hands. The story of the whole alliance is told under Aztec Triple Alliance.
